# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Total Hip Replacement (CPT 27130)

**Emerson Alvarez**
[Street address]
[City], MO [ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Submitted online at my.cigna.com or by phone at 1-800-244-6224

---

**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-09**

- **Member name:** Emerson Alvarez
- **Member ID:** W977514824
- **Reference number:** POC-4E415360FE-32022
- **Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), state of Missouri
- **Service denied:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
- **Governing policy:** *Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026*, effective 2026-08-04 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-313%20Hip%20Replace%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my total hip replacement (CPT 27130) and asking Cigna to reconsider that decision and authorize the surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-09 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am writing because the records already in my file address the criteria in the plan's own policy, and I would like a reviewer to look at them point by point. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is needed.

I am submitting this appeal within the time frame stated in my denial notice, which says my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-05**. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and/or filing it through my.cigna.com.

Below, I quote the plan's published criteria exactly and then point to what my records say. All of the quoted language comes from *Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026*.

---

## The plan's criteria, matched to my records

### 1. Imaging

The policy states:

> "Imaging shows ANY of the following findings:"

The excerpts of the policy available to me include these findings:

> "Tönnis Grade 2-3 osteoarthritis"

> "avascular necrosis with collapse of the femoral head"

> "inflammatory arthritis affecting BOTH the femoral head and the acetabulum with joint space narrowing"

This part of the policy introduces a list, and I have not been given the full list, so there may be additional imaging findings the policy accepts that I cannot see. I am asking Cigna to tell me which imaging criterion it applied to my request.

**What my records show:** A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph dated 2026-06-02 shows the hip joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. My records do not assign a Tönnis grade to that film. If a graded reading is what the reviewer is looking for, that is a document request rather than a reason to deny, and I ask that Cigna say so plainly so Dr. Lindqvist can provide it. The imaging itself was submitted and is in my file.

The policy also contains a separate pathway referring to when "Imaging shows a fracture of the femoral head or femoral neck." and when "Conservative management or surgical fixation is not considered a reasonable option." That is not my situation; my request falls under the category the policy describes as "Osteoarthritis, Avascular Necrosis (AVN), Inflammatory Arthritis".

### 2. Symptoms

The policy states:

> "Symptoms include BOTH of the following:"

The first is:

> "function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration"

**What my records show:** I have had 24 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. I walk with a cane and am limited to one block. That is a longer duration and a shorter walking distance than the example the policy itself gives.

The second is:

> "loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

**What my records show:** I cannot put on my own shoes without help, and I use a cane to get around. My exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

### 3. Non-surgical management

The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

**What my records show:**

- Supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait: 16 weeks, from 2026-03-03 to 2026-06-23, with 20 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-15, which gave 3 weeks of partial relief.

The physical therapy course alone spans 16 weeks, which is longer than the three-month duration the policy names, and it was provider-directed and documented. The medication trial and the injection are in the record as well.

The policy also provides:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of function-limiting pain is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate."

and

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate."

I note these exceptions only for completeness. I do not need to rely on them, because my records document both the pain duration and a completed course of non-surgical management that exceeds three months.

### 4. Preoperative optimization

The policy includes this note:

> "Note: It is incumbent on the surgeon to preoperatively optimize reasonably modifiable medical and behavioral health comorbidities."

**What my records show:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and I am a non-smoker.

---

## Why I am asking for reconsideration

The reason given on the notice is that the documentation was incomplete. The notice does not tell me which specific item was missing or which criterion could not be evaluated. The records already submitted include the dated radiograph and its findings, the dated physical therapy course with visit count and discharge note, the medication and injection history with dates, my walking limitation and use of a cane, my exam findings, and my comorbidity status.

If a particular document is still needed, I am glad to obtain it. I am asking Cigna to:

1. Identify the specific criterion in *Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026* that it applied, and the specific document or finding it considers missing;
2. Provide me the full list of imaging findings under the criterion quoted above, since the excerpt available to me ends at a colon and the list is not reproduced;
3. Review the records described in this letter against those criteria and overturn the denial and authorize CPT 27130.

I would also like the appeal to include a review by a physician with orthopedic experience, and I am requesting a free copy of the clinical criteria and any reviewer notes used to make this decision.

Documents I am enclosing or asking Cigna to pull from my file:

- Denial notice dated 2026-08-09, reference POC-4E415360FE-32022
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph and report dated 2026-06-02
- Physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-03-03 to 2026-06-23
- Office notes from Dr. Lindqvist, orthopedic surgery, documenting symptoms, exam, and the recommendation for surgery
- [Any additional records my surgeon's office sends under separate cover]

Thank you for taking another look at this. I am living with pain that limits me to one block of walking and keeps me from dressing myself, and my surgeon has documented that this surgery is needed. Please contact me at [phone] or [email] if anything further would help.

Sincerely,

**Emerson Alvarez**
Member ID: W977514824
